Today (the 17th), a netizen uploaded a video on social media showing closed-circuit television footage of a back alley where three people were seen talking on site. At least two people wearing Food and Environmental Hygiene Department uniforms can be clearly seen in the footage. Based on information about FEHD uniforms, these two are suspected to be a hawker management officer and a senior hawker management officer respectively.

The footage shows two officer-level personnel chatting in the back alley, with one of them first taking out a cigarette to smoke. Afterwards, another senior hawker management officer walked over, took out a cigarette case and a lighter, flicked through his hair lightly, put a cigarette into his mouth, and walked away with his back to the camera, with light smoke drifting around him during that time.

Citizen News inquired with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department whether the people in the video were FEHD personnel. In response to the inquiry, the department confirmed that the people in the video were personnel from the FEHD's district hawker management teams. A spokesperson said the incident occurred in early June this year. The reporter asked whether FEHD personnel are allowed to smoke while wearing uniform? If the video is genuine, did the personnel involved violate any rules? Would this affect the department's image? The FEHD replied that, according to the department's current regulations, personnel are strictly prohibited from smoking while in uniform and in public places.

The FEHD stated that the department attaches great importance to staff discipline and professional conduct, has commenced a disciplinary investigation into the incident, and will take appropriate action in accordance with established procedures and the findings of the investigation. The spokesperson also pointed out that the department has clear requirements regarding the conduct of personnel while in uniform, and any behaviour that violates departmental disciplinary requirements will be followed up seriously.
